g.text: Broad Run: four independent sources, one basin

text.style: font-size: 9px; font-family: 'Helvetica Neue', 'Helvetica', 'Arial', 'DejaVu Sans', sans-serif; text-anchor: start; fill: #52514e

g.text: The basin carrying 72.5% of Prince William County's data centers

text.style: font-size: 6.9px; font-family: 'Helvetica Neue', 'Helvetica', 'Arial', 'DejaVu Sans', sans-serif; fill: #898781

g.text: Concentration is the county's own watershed layer crossed with the building attribution. The flow denominator comes from a gage decommissioned in

text.style: font-size: 6.9px; font-family: 'Helvetica Neue', 'Helvetica', 'Arial', 'DejaVu Sans', sans-serif; fill: #898781

g.text: 1986, which never observed any part of the drought now underway. Of 17 stream stations in the Prince William / Occoquan group, 15 have positive

text.style: font-size: 6.9px; font-family: 'Helvetica Neue', 'Helvetica', 'Arial', 'DejaVu Sans', sans-serif; fill: #898781

g.text: temperature trends, 1 is exactly zero and 1 negative (sign test on the 16 non-ties: p = 0.0005); Broad Run 1ABRB002.15 is the only one individually

text.style: font-size: 6.9px; font-family: 'Helvetica Neue', 'Helvetica', 'Arial', 'DejaVu Sans', sans-serif; fill: #898781

g.text: significant at p<0.05. Statewide only 49 of 413 stations are

text.style: font-size: 6.9px; font-family: 'Helvetica Neue', 'Helvetica', 'Arial', 'DejaVu Sans', sans-serif; fill: #898781

g.text: significant — but 47 of those 49 are warming and 2 cooling. The PDSI series is the observed NOAA/NCEI county record, not a projection.
